rejected.title: Analysing language for persuasive effect
card: A persuasive technique is a choice of language meant to influence the reader, such as emotive words, a statistic or a rhetorical question.
Good analysis names the technique and quotes a few of the writer's words. Keep the quote short and fit it into your own sentence.
Then it explains the effect: how the technique is meant to make the audience feel or think, so that they lean towards the writer's side.
Example: a writer calls a new road "a scar across the valley". The metaphor suggests harm and damage, so readers may feel protective of the valley and oppose the road.
rejected.remember: Name the technique, quote the words, then explain how they position the reader.

a.q: A writer says teenagers are "drowning in screens". Which sentence is the best analysis of this language?
opts: The metaphor "drowning" implies danger, so parents may act
The writer uses the metaphor "drowning" about teenagers
The metaphor "drowning" shows the writer dislikes phones
The writer argues that teenagers spend too long on screens
a.why: It names the metaphor, quotes the word "drowning" and explains how readers are meant to react: seeing danger, parents may want to act. The option that only says the writer uses a metaphor names and quotes but stops before the effect, so it is not full analysis.
a.clue: Which option says what the reader may think or do?

b.q: Mia writes that her town's library, "a place of quiet and hope", is being shut. Which analysis best explains the persuasive effect of the emotive words?
opts: "Quiet and hope" stir warmth, so readers may oppose closure
"Quiet and hope" are two nouns that describe the library
"Quiet and hope" show how much Mia herself loves the library
"Quiet and hope" are facts, so readers will trust Mia
b.why: The right analysis links the words to a feeling in the reader and to the stance they may take on the closure. The option about how much Mia loves the library is tempting, but it explains the writer's feelings, not how the audience is positioned. Calling the words two nouns only describes them and never reaches an effect.
b.clue: Effect is about the audience, not the writer.

a.q: Which sentence is the best piece of analysis of the phrase "a scar across the valley"?
opts: The metaphor suggests harm, so readers may oppose the road
The writer uses a metaphor in the sentence about the road
The writer talks about a road that crosses a valley
The phrase is descriptive and helps the reader picture it
a.why: It names the technique, uses the writer's words and explains how the reader is positioned. The option that only names a metaphor stops before the effect, which is the tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Which option explains the effect on the reader?

b.q: Mia writes that her town's library, "a place of quiet and hope", is being shut. Which analysis best explains the persuasive effect of the emotive words?
opts: "Quiet and hope" bring warm feelings, so readers may resent the closure
"Quiet and hope" are two nouns that describe the library
The emotive words show how much Mia likes books and reading
"Quiet and hope" are facts, so readers will trust Mia's claim
b.why: The first option links the words to a feeling and to the reader's likely response. The second only describes the words and never reaches an effect. The third is about the writer's feelings, not the audience, which is a common slip.
b.clue: Look for the option that links the words to the reader's reaction.
